_readme: William's decisions from import-report.md. warband_aliases: a source warband name -> type slugs ([] leaves it out); MiM restrictions use them too; one that keeps the mapping the build would make reads as settled in the report. extra_warband_types: warbands neither Broheim nor mordheimer lists (its setting and source, and its grade and Broheim PDF where it has them). drop_warband_types: a Broheim warband left out -> why (one William split into two, whose types are extra_warband_types entries); the seeder archives the type it drops. warband_type_names: a type's name as Broheim spells it -> as we show it (a typo or a capital "Of"; the slug stays the source's). persona_item_names: a name a dramatis persona's kit prints -> our item it means, for one that is ours under another word (Heinrich 'Altdorf' Schmidt's Whip is our Steel Whip; the Khemri equipment page prints no whip of its own, 11 Nov 2026). persona_names: a dramatis persona's name as mordheimer gives it -> ours (one casing: title case, small words lower case after the first; William, 5 Nov 2026). group_members: add/remove type slugs per group slug, and keep_in/keep_out the types William keeps in or out of a group (held there); each settles its types' group questions. setting_grades: setting slug -> grade. keep_hidden_items: mordheimer items it hides that should be imported anyway. drop_items: mordheimer items left out. item_names: a mordheimer item's name -> the name we show it under (name), the tags added with it (tags), the tags dropped (drop_tags), the kind and subtype it takes (type, subtype: the Magic Carpet is an Animal, a Mount, since the bestiary holds it), the range, strength or save it takes where mordheimer's is wrong (the Nehekharan Javelins' 8", 12" in their warband's own PDF) and why. item_warbands: item name -> the only type slugs that may buy it, and why. item_warbands_add: item name -> type slugs added to its mordheimer list, and why. item_exclusions: item name -> the only type slugs an item for everyone shuts out, and why. item_defaults_kept: item name -> why the default its contradictions took stands. item_own_rules: our item's name -> the rules William settles for it (rules: name, summary, text), in place of its own. item_notes: item name -> a soft note added to each of its price rows. item_rule_wordings: a shared item rule's slug -> the wording William settles for it (summary, text), the items whose own wording it now covers (covers: their own is dropped) and those that keep only what is theirs (items: name -> summary, text). whole_names: names matched as a whole on the same-name list, not split at the slash. setting_assignments: kind (skills, hired_swords, dramatis_personae) -> our row's name as the report shows it ("Sniper (Hochland Bandits)") -> setting slug (one mordheimer gives several settings is then settled). skill_lists: a skill list's name -> who learns the skills of it mordheimer lacks (for_everyone, or warbands as {type} or {group} slugs), large_only (a Large unit's skill) and a note shown when learning. drop_skills: our skill rows left out (label -> why). extra_skills: skill rows our table lacks. skill_descriptions: a skill row's description put right (label -> text). fees_in_rules: a hired sword's or dramatis persona's name -> why its hire fee is in its rules: kind special, its gold kept, its hiring sentence in full as the note. hire_warbands_add: a hired sword's or dramatis persona's name -> type slugs added to its mordheimer hire list, and why (a list that then matches a group is stored as that group, so it follows the group). Skill groups (phase 1a): our skill rows merge by name into one skill each, linked into the group of every list that had it, and each list is a group; a list's skill_lists decision is its group's (who learns from it, large_only, note). skill_splits: a row (by label) whose rule differs stays its own skill under name, in its group alone, and why. skill_wordings: a merged skill's name -> the wording it takes (text, or the row label it is from) and why; any other merged skill keeps its longest. skill_group_learners: a group's name -> who learns from it (for_everyone, or warbands as {type} or {group} slugs), settling a group the report flags (its default is the warbands that may learn every skill in it). new_skill_groups: groups our lists lack -> the warband type that alone learns from it (type, or types), our skills it holds (skills) and new ones (new_skills; {name, rule} names one apart from the skill whose rules it takes) with rules from mordheimer, or from the source file in sources/ it names. seed_items_back: an item of our old seed (apps/items/data/standard-items.json) -> the setting and source it comes back with, and why: its price rows and properties as they were, single use kept. extra_items: items no source has: name, type, subtype, setting, source, link_url, flavour, cost (with dice and dice_multiplier for a dice price: 10+4D6 is cost 10, dice 4) and rarity, a statblock for an animal sold as an item, the warband types that buy it (none: everyone), the price row's note, its rules (a shared rule by slug, or its own) and why. warband_items: an item a warband's special equipment brings in (warband_items.py) -> the snapshot page (testwarbands-2026-10-31), the entry when it is named otherwise, the warband type that buys it, its type and subtype: one price row for that type at the book's price and rarity. mim_merges: a Mutiny in Marienburg stub that duplicates a complete item of ours -> the item it joins (item), the tags carried with it (tags) and why; the stub is left out and the book's price becomes a price row of that item labelled "Mutiny in Marienburg", since a price row has no setting of its own (William, 15 Nov 2026). single_use_items: the items a battle uses up (William, 26 Nov 2026), each marked single_use on every variant; a name that is no item stops the build. item_splits: a book item split into items of its own (William, 26 Nov 2026: Club, Mace or Hammer) -> the new items with their tags (items: name -> tags; everything else is the original's), the one every warband list that sold it now sells (default) and the templates that sell another (templates: slug -> item and why); the original is dropped, so the seeder archives it, and its lines keep their price, who and limits (item_splits.py). An item, template or choice that matches nothing stops the build. item_saves: an item's name -> what equipping it does to the wearer's armour save (bonus: the steps it moves it, read from the save it prints with no save as 7+, so a 6+ item is 1 and a 4+ item 3; slot: body, shield, mount or extra, where only one body item counts at a time), and the subtype it shows under. William, 18 Nov 2026: "Armour items should be viewed as +1 (light), +2 (heavy) etc but if a piece of armoud is equipped already then ignore subsequent. taking it away should just minus that value up to 6+. Helmets do nothing. Things like shields and mounting a mount when equipped should plus their value and take away when unequipped, no checks needed on these its up to user to be normal." A save a condition qualifies takes no bonus, with `why` instead: one number can't hold the condition, so the item's rules text does the work. A mount's bonus is its kind's, not data (apps/bestiary/animal_items.py). item_subtypes: a subtype one source spells its own way -> the subtype we show it under, so one kind sits under one subtype (William, 25 Nov 2026: Missile is Ranged, Drug/Poison is Poisons and Drugs, Vehicle/Watercraft is Vehicles).

rules.summary: Thrown; D3 S4 hits with no armour save, S3 within 1"
rules.text: A fire bomb is thrown in the shooting phase, with a range of twice the thrower's Strength in inches. Roll to hit with his Ballistic Skill, with no modifier for range or moving. A hit causes D3 Strength 4 hits with no armour save, and every warrior within 1", friend or foe, takes one Strength 3 hit with saves as normal. On a roll of 1 to hit, the bomb misfires and explodes as though it had hit the thrower.

Fire Bomb.why: The Innocents PDF (p8) prints the fire bomb's rules and ours had none

rules.summary: Thrown as an enemy charges; he strikes last unless he passes an Initiative test
rules.text: A smoke bomb may be thrown as an enemy charges the wielder, interrupting the charge. The charger is placed in base contact and must pass an Initiative test at once. If he fails he is blinded and strikes last in the hand-to-hand combat phase whatever his Initiative or his skills.

Smoke Bomb.why: The Innocents PDF (p8) prints the smoke bomb's rules and ours had none

rules.summary: Keeps the wearer's equipment dry; over armour, never with a cloak
rules.text: A rain coat keeps its wearer, and above all his equipment and his blackpowder, dry in wet weather. It may be worn over armour with no penalty, but never together with a cloak, and it is no help against the water a model walks or falls into. It is an exception to the normal rules, in that a Henchman may have one.

Rain Coat.why: William, 11 Nov 2026: the Sartosa Greatcoat is our Rain Coat ("Based on 'Raincoat' from Border Town Burning", 10 gc), and its two clauses - worn over armour but not with a cloak, and no help in water terrain - fold into ours, which said only that a Henchman may have one and left what it does to its flavour line

rules.summary: Flying mount with 16" movement; destroyed outright by fire
rules.text: A magic carpet is indeed just that – a carpet that flies! It counts as a mount and allows movement of 16" with no restrictions for terrain. You can move onto the roofs of buildings and other high places with no penalty. The carpet may carry up to three men or one large creature and a man. One of the riders must be a character. Due to its magical nature it cannot be destroyed, except by fire: taken out of action by fire it is destroyed outright, with no roll on the Henchmen injury chart.

Magic Carpet.why: William, 12 Nov 2026: the Khemri equipment page destroys the carpet by fire where ours said only that its magical nature means it cannot be destroyed, so the fire rule is added to ours; the bestiary mount already carried it

rules.summary: Strength test to acquire; +1 armour save against shooting
rules.text: To acquire the cloak a warrior must pay 10 gc, for the travel and the hunt, and roll equal to or under his Strength on a D6. If he succeeds he finds and slays the beast and wears its cloak. A warband whose own equipment list sells the cloak may buy one when the warband is raised without testing for availability. A model wearing it gains +1 to his armour saves against all shooting attacks.

rules.name: Critical Damage
rules.text: Dark Elf Blades inflict serious damage on their opponents. When rolling on the critical hit chart a Dark Elf Blade will add +1 to the result.

rules.name: Wicked Edge
rules.text: Dark Elf Blades are set with sharp protrusions and serrated edges which inflict serious damage on an opponent. A roll of 2-4 on the injury table is a Stunned result.

rules.name: Swords and daggers only
rules.summary: Only a sword or a dagger may have one
rules.text: Only a sword or a dagger may be made with one of these blades.

rules.summary: Open doors using Initiative instead of Strength
rules.text: A model equipped with a set of lock picks may make his test to open doors on his Initiative rather than his Strength characteristic if he wishes. This is done at the end of his Movement phase as if the model were ripping the door off its hinges, though he uses his Initiative rather than Strength, without the -2 to the test, and there is no chance that the door is too damaged to be locked again later.

rules.summary: Never gain experience, same recovery chance as Henchmen
rules.text: Wardogs never gain experience, and if they are put out of action they have exactly the same chance of recovering as Henchmen (ie, 1-2: Dead; 3-6: Alive).

rules.summary: Counts towards maximum warriors in warband
rules.text: Wardogs count towards the maximum number of warriors allowed in your warband.

extra_skills.name: Starstruck

extra_skills.name: Rough and Tumble

extra_skills.name: Axe Thrower
extra_skills.description: The warrior is a master of the throwing axe. He may throw up to two Throwing Axes in his shooting phase and may divide the shots between any targets in range as he wishes, each attack at +1 Strength. He must own Throwing Axes to use it, and it may not be combined with Quick Shot.
extra_skills.source: the Sartosa campaign rules' Skills PDF (Broheim, Sartosa), New Shooting Skill

extra_skills.name: Bulwark
extra_skills.description: A warrior armed with a single-handed weapon (sword, spear, hammer and the like) and a shield has an additional +1 on his armour saving roll in close combat.
extra_skills.source: the Mutiny in Marienburg main document (Broheim, Mutiny in Marienburg), Epic Campaign Rules, New skills

extra_skills.name: Lunge
extra_skills.description: With a spear or a dagger the warrior may strike foes that would normally be out of reach: when he charges, move him 1" further forward. A lunge can only be avoided with the Step Aside skill on a roll of 6, and armour saves apply as normal.
extra_skills.source: the Mutiny in Marienburg main document (Broheim, Mutiny in Marienburg), Epic Campaign Rules, New skills

extra_skills.name: Target Practice
extra_skills.description: The warrior may fire a single missile attack when he is charged. A model that stands and shoots is at -1 to hit.
extra_skills.source: the Mutiny in Marienburg main document (Broheim, Mutiny in Marienburg), Epic Campaign Rules, New skills

extra_skills.name: Crossfire
extra_skills.description: The Hero may use missile weapons while in close combat, shooting at enemy models not in that combat, at -1 to hit for moving. Friendly models in the way are ignored when checking line of sight.
extra_skills.source: the Mutiny in Marienburg main document (Broheim, Mutiny in Marienburg), Epic Campaign Rules, New skills

extra_skills.name: Hunter's Eye
extra_skills.description: Once per game the Hero may make as many ranged attacks in the turn as he has close combat attacks.
extra_skills.source: the Mutiny in Marienburg main document (Broheim, Mutiny in Marienburg), Epic Campaign Rules, New skills

extra_skills.name: Pilot
extra_skills.description: A boat piloted by the Hero may re-roll results on the Propulsion Damage chart once. The second result must be accepted even if it is worse.
extra_skills.source: the Mutiny in Marienburg main document (Broheim, Mutiny in Marienburg), Epic Campaign Rules, New skills

extra_skills.name: Dirty Blow
extra_skills.description: The attack ignores armour, but no weapon bonus and no Strength modifier applies to it.
extra_skills.source: the Mutiny in Marienburg main document (Broheim, Mutiny in Marienburg), Epic Campaign Rules, New skills

extra_skills.name: Rigger
extra_skills.description: The Hero is skilled in fixing minor damage to watercraft. If the boat or barge is stationary and did not move last turn, and the Hero is in contact with it, he may repair one location previously damaged or set on fire, such as a paddle or a mast. He may do nothing else that turn and the boat may not move. It cannot be repaired while an enemy model is in contact with the Hero or the watercraft.
extra_skills.source: the Mutiny in Marienburg main document (Broheim, Mutiny in Marienburg), Epic Campaign Rules, New skills

extra_skills.name: Tunnel Rat
extra_skills.description: Any characteristic test the Hero takes in a scenario set in the sewers or elsewhere underground may be re-rolled.
extra_skills.source: the Mutiny in Marienburg main document (Broheim, Mutiny in Marienburg), Epic Campaign Rules, New skills

extra_skills.name: Spry

extra_skills.source: the Mutiny in Marienburg main document (Broheim, Mutiny in Marienburg), Epic Campaign Rules, New skills

extra_skills.name: Martyr
extra_skills.description: The warrior doesn't fear death, knowing that his god has decided in advance when he will die, and he inspires his comrades. While he is in close combat he gains the Leader skill. Every time he rolls on the Serious Injury chart he gains +1 experience point.
extra_skills.source: the Relics of the Crusades Part 1 PDF (Broheim, Relics of the Crusades), New skills & spells, Holy Skills

extra_skills.name: Charitable
extra_skills.description: The warrior indulges in charitable works and shuns money, so the poor of the towns follow him, aiding in any way they can. D3 mace-armed Novices (see the Sisters of Sigmar warband) accompany him in every battle and don't count towards the warband's limit. However, just before each battle he spends D6x5 dinars on the poor, and sells all of his equipment if the warband doesn't have the funds to pay.
extra_skills.source: the Relics of the Crusades Part 1 PDF (Broheim, Relics of the Crusades), New skills & spells, Holy Skills

extra_skills.name: Slayer of the Heretic
extra_skills.description: The warrior hates everyone who follows a path different to his. The warband must execute any prisoners he hates, and may not use Hired Swords or Dramatis Personae, as he will not suffer their blasphemous ways.
extra_skills.source: the Relics of the Crusades Part 1 PDF (Broheim, Relics of the Crusades), New skills & spells, Holy Skills

extra_skills.name: Aesthete
extra_skills.description: The warrior gives up his possessions, trusting in his god to protect him. His only possession is a staff (a mace or a double-handed weapon, as chosen). He passes any Leadership test (not Rout tests) and gains an unmodified 5+ save against any wound.
extra_skills.source: the Relics of the Crusades Part 1 PDF (Broheim, Relics of the Crusades), New skills & spells, Holy Skills

extra_skills.name: Light of Glory
extra_skills.description: A halo of light surrounds the warrior's head, which the undead shun instinctively. Undead fear the warrior (an exception to the Undead's immunity to psychology). The halo also acts as a light source in the same way as a torch.
extra_skills.source: the Relics of the Crusades Part 1 PDF (Broheim, Relics of the Crusades), New skills & spells, Holy Skills

extra_skills.name: Divine Guidance
extra_skills.description: The warrior performs a dangerous pilgrimage to attract his god's blessings. He must miss the next game and roll once on the Serious Injury chart. He can then roll for one spell from the Divine Interventions list.
extra_skills.source: the Relics of the Crusades Part 1 PDF (Broheim, Relics of the Crusades), New skills & spells, Holy Skills

extra_skills.name: On the Wings of Angels

extra_skills.source: the Relics of the Crusades Part 1 PDF (Broheim, Relics of the Crusades), New skills & spells, Holy Skills

extra_skills.name: Converter
extra_skills.description: During the post-battle sequence roll a D6: on a 6 the warrior has convinced a peasant to join the cause, and you may add a Novice (see the Sisters of Sigmar warband) to the warband as a new henchman. If the warband captures an enemy who isn't on the same path as the warband, the warrior may try to convert him: after every game roll 2D6 for the converter and for the captive, each adding his Leadership. If the captive scores higher he remains a prisoner; if the converter scores higher, the prisoner joins and fights for the warband with all of his original equipment.

extra_skills.name: Blessed Weapon

extra_skills.source: the Relics of the Crusades Part 1 PDF (Broheim, Relics of the Crusades), New skills & spells, Holy Skills

extra_skills.name: Iron Faith
extra_skills.description: The warrior is steadfast against the deceitfulness of sorcery, and gains an unmodified 5+ save against any spell that affects him.
extra_skills.source: the Relics of the Crusades Part 1 PDF (Broheim, Relics of the Crusades), New skills & spells, Holy Skills

extra_skills.name: Smith
extra_skills.description: Before each game he takes part in, the warrior may work on one close combat weapon or suit of heavy armour. The wielder of a smithed weapon may re-roll the first failed to-hit roll of the battle; the bearer of smithed armour may re-roll the first failed armour save.

extra_skills.description: The warrior is practised at fighting with two weapons and ignores the -1 to hit the Annual's Dual Wielding rule gives each attack made with two weapons. Under that rule a hired sword who comes with two or more weapons counts as having this skill.

extra_skills.name: Splintering Blow
extra_skills.description: The warrior's axe blows tear through armour: every axe he fights with has an armour save modifier of -2.

extra_skills.name: Beat Down
extra_skills.description: When the warrior fights with a morning star or flail of any kind and wounds an enemy in the first round of a combat, he keeps the weapon's Strength bonus into the next round, and goes on keeping it for every round in which he wounds an opponent.

extra_skills.name: Fortitude

extra_skills.name: Impressive Bulk
extra_skills.description: Whenever the Hero takes a Strength or Toughness test, that characteristic counts as 1 higher for the test.

extra_skills.source: the Marienburg Annual (Broheim, Mutiny in Marienburg), New Skills, Combat Skills (p. 9)

extra_skills.description: The warrior shrugs off blows that would fell a lesser fighter: when he suffers a critical wound, the attacker is at -1 on the critical hit chart.

skill_descriptions.Quick Thinker (Dwarf Exiled Engineers): The dwarf may add +1 to any roll on the experimental weapons chart. (MiM)
skill_descriptions.Trap Expert (Academic): This Hero is able to detect traps in the tombs with relative ease. A character who possesses this skill will never set off traps himself (but may be subject to their effects if he is too close when it goes off). He can attempt to disarm traps by stopping at the trap during his Movement phase, and may do nothing else that turn. To disarm a Simple trap, roll 6+ on 2D6. To disarm a Complex trap, roll 8+ on 2D6. If unsuccessful, he must test against his Initiative; a failed test means he sets off the trap himself. He can also attempt to restore dud or previously de-activated traps: roll a D6 (1-4 Simple, 5-6 Complex), then roll 6+ on 2D6 to restore a Simple trap or 8+ on 2D6 for a Complex trap. Failure means the trap fails to activate. Either half may be taken up to four times, taking 1 off its roll each time, so that at the limit a Simple trap is disarmed on a 2+ and a Complex trap on a 4+.
skill_descriptions.Mutant (Beastmen Raiders): The Hero may buy one mutation from the Possessed Mutation list. This skill may be taken only once. (EiF 74)
skill_descriptions.Ignore Pain (Skaven Clan Pestilens): A Clan Pestilens member with this skill treats “Stunned” injuries as “Knocked Down.” (TC 29)
skill_descriptions.Handyman (Strength): The warrior is skilled in fixing minor damage on a wagon, cart or coach. If the wagon is stationary and has not moved during the last turn then if the warrior is in contact with the wagon, he may repair one previously damaged wheel. He can even set in a new wheel if it flew off. The Hero may do nothing else that turn and the wagon may not be moved. A wagon cannot be repaired if an enemy model is in contact with the handyman or the wagon. (MiM)
skill_descriptions.Beastmaster (Strength): The Hero is able to communicate on a primal level with any beast he encounters. If the model confronts an animal (not mount) in hand-to-hand combat, before combat he may take a Leadership test. If the test fails, combat proceeds as normal. If successful the animal falls under his command. Place the models 1" apart. The player may control the animal, but the beastmaster must pass a Leadership test at the beginning of his turn or control is lost. The animal must remain within 6" of the Hero or control is lost. No more than one animal can be controlled this way. (MiM)
skill_descriptions.Sniper (Shadow Warriors): If Hidden, a warrior with this skill may shoot or cast spells and still remain Hidden. (TC10) If the sniper’s target is not taken out of action he is allowed an immediate Initiative test, as is anyone within 2” of him, and if successful they spot the sniper and he loses his ability to remain Hidden. (TC 12)
skill_descriptions.Wall Runner (Skaven): The warrior does not need to take an Initiative test when climbing up walls and other sheer surfaces. (RB 93)

rules.text:
Choose a warrior with a serious injury he wants mended, then roll a D6 for how the surgery goes.

{{table:1}}

rows: Pray harder: the warrior must have displeased the gods, as there are complications during the surgery. Roll on the Serious Injuries chart for the unfortunate Hero and apply the result.
The One's will: the physician declares that The One has decreed in advance that you would not be cured today. The surgery has no benefit.
I thought I sterilised that...: the surgeon cures the injury, but there are complications. Replace the injury with Old Battle Wound.
By the will of The One!: the surgery is a success. Remove the serious injury from the warrior.

extra_items.flavour: Great creatures, known as the Ships of the Desert can go for days without water and carry great burdens without fatigue. The Arabians would load one up with water that could last for days.

rules.text: For each ship of the desert it has, a warband can ignore the effects of horribly hot and burning sands for five of its members.

extra_items.why: Relics of the Crusades pp. 4-5 and 15: 100+2D6 dinars, Rare 7 at Dimashque (Rare 8 at Khalibon, in the note) (William, 21 Nov 2026: "Relics yes, bring items and skills and spells in")

extra_items.name: Master Astrologer
extra_items.flavour: The journals of those present during these times tell of magicians who could divine the future by analysing the heavens. It seems most were charlatans hoping to make a quick dinar from passing fools. However, it is rumoured that in some towns there were seers who could guide men to what they truly desired.
extra_items.note: Not available to warbands on the Path of Sigmar. Khalibon: 25+3D6 dinars, Rare 8.

rules.text: For the next D3 games the warband fights in a desert locale, it may roll an extra D6 during exploration, and this D6 may be modified by +1 or -1.

rules.name: Charlatan
rules.text: If the warband fails the rarity roll, it has met a charlatan instead. Its leader must take an Initiative test. If he fails, the warband pays the price as if it had found the master astrologer, and rolls on the Lost in the Desert table, applying the result to its next battle.

extra_items.why: Relics of the Crusades pp. 4-5 and 15: 25+3D6 dinars, Rare 9 at Dimashque (Rare 8 at Khalibon, in the note); not for the Path of Sigmar, a path rather than a warband type, so the note says so (William, 21 Nov 2026: "Relics yes, bring items and skills and spells in")

extra_items.name: Magic Tattoo
extra_items.flavour: The knowledge of engraving a magical tattoo into skin is a combination of the arcane knowledge of many races, including dwarven rune smithing and the “arts” of the savage orcs.

rules.text: A hero who buys a magic tattoo chooses one spell from the Lesser Magic list, and may now cast it. Finding an artist who lets him choose from Necromancy, Chaos Rituals or Blessings of Nurgle adds +2 to the tattoo's rarity, taking it over 13, so the hero must have the Streetwise skill or something similar to get one.

extra_items.why: Relics of the Crusades pp. 5 and 15: 200+D6x25 dinars, Rare 11, sold only at Khalibon (William, 21 Nov 2026: "Relics yes, bring items and skills and spells in")

extra_items.name: Vermin Pot
extra_items.flavour: Vermin pots were invented by the ancient Khemrians and were in use during the crusades. Biting, poisonous insects were placed into ceramic pots then sealed within and kept alive by tiny air holes and a piece of rotten meat. When thrown, the vermin pot would smash to pieces and release the angry creatures within.

rules.text: Models using vermin pots do not suffer penalties for range or moving.

rules.name: Thrown Pot
rules.text: A vermin pot is a ranged weapon the character rolls to hit with as normal. If it hits, the pot lands on the target. If he misses, the pot lands D6" away from the target in a random direction.

rules.name: Vermin
rules.text: If the pot hits, place a vermin swarm in base contact with the target: it counts as charging in the close combat that follows. If it misses, place the swarm where the pot lands. The swarm charges and moves to get into close combat with the closest warrior, members of the thrower's warband included.

extra_items.why: Relics of the Crusades pp. 4-5 and 15: 30+2D6 dinars, Rare 9 at Dimashque (25+D6, Rare 8 at Khalibon, in the note); range Strength x 2 inches (William, 21 Nov 2026: "Relics yes, bring items and skills and spells in")

extra_items.name: Dimashquine Blade
extra_items.flavour: These are another secret of the Arabians that has passed into mystery. Dimashquine blades were reputed to be strong enough to cut through the swords of their enemies like they were pig’s cheese.

rules.text: A Dimashquine blade counts as a sword.
If its wielder scores 5+ on his parry roll, the weapon his opponent is attacking him with is destroyed. Only weapons of Common availability can be destroyed this way.

extra_items.why: Relics of the Crusades pp. 4 and 15: 15+2D6 dinars, Rare 9, sold only at Dimashque; it counts as a sword, so the sword's Parry (William, 21 Nov 2026: "Relics yes, bring items and skills and spells in")

extra_items.name: Stickfire Pot
extra_items.flavour: The secret of creating stickfire is now lost though it was well documented that it was used by Arabian defenders during the crusades.

rules.text: Models using stickfire pots do not suffer penalties for range or moving.

rules.name: Thrown Pot
rules.text: A stickfire pot is a ranged weapon the character rolls to hit with as normal. If it hits, the pot lands on the target, who is covered in stickfire. If he misses, the pot lands D6" away from the target in a random direction, and anyone it lands on is covered in stickfire. The warrior has enough pots for one battle.

rules.name: Stickfire
rules.text: All models within 1" of a model covered in stickfire at the beginning of a turn count as being on fire and suffer a Strength 4 hit. A warrior who survives must score a 4+ in the Recovery phase or suffer a Strength 4 hit each turn he is on fire, and moves D6" in a random direction. Other warriors cannot help to put out the flames, as they are too afraid. If a warrior carrying stickfire pots ever catches on fire, all his stickfire pots are destroyed, and he automatically suffers D3 Strength 5 hits as the flammable materials explode.

extra_items.why: Relics of the Crusades pp. 4-5 and 16: 35+2D6 dinars, Rare 10 at Dimashque, printed Stickfire Pots (35+D6, Rare 12 at Khalibon, in the note); range Strength x 2 inches (William, 21 Nov 2026: "Relics yes, bring items and skills and spells in")

extra_items.name: Stickfire Hose
extra_items.flavour: A dastardly invention, the stickfire hose was carried by a team that shot flaming stickfire at their enemies. Launched by a series of pumps or bellows, the stickfire would cover and burn all in its path.

rules.text: You may not move and fire a stickfire hose in the same turn, other than to pivot on the spot to face your target or stand up from being knocked down.

rules.name: Large and Complex
rules.text: It takes two warriors to carry a stickfire hose, and they must stay in base contact throughout the game. There is only enough stickfire for D3 uses, rolled after the first shot.

rules.name: Dangerous
rules.text: Henchmen may use a stickfire hose, as its instability makes any hero wary of holding it.

rules.name: Stream
rules.text: When the hose fires, draw a line 16" long and 1" wide in any direction from the firer (absolutely straight). Every model in its path is automatically hit by stickfire.

rules.name: Stickfire
rules.text: All models within 1" of a model covered in stickfire at the beginning of a turn count as being on fire and suffer a Strength 4 hit. A warrior who survives must score a 4+ in the Recovery phase or suffer a Strength 4 hit each turn he is on fire, and moves D6" in a random direction. Other warriors cannot help to put out the flames, as they are too afraid. If a warrior carrying a stickfire hose ever catches on fire, the hose is destroyed and removed from his equipment, and he automatically suffers D3 Strength 5 hits as the flammable materials explode.

extra_items.why: Relics of the Crusades pp. 4 and 16: 190+D6x10 dinars, Rare 11, sold only at Dimashque; Henchmen may use it, so no Heroes only note (William, 21 Nov 2026: "Relics yes, bring items and skills and spells in")

extra_items.name: Perfume
extra_items.flavour: Used by the wealthiest merchants in Araby, perfume showed that the wearer had noble tastes.

rules.text: A character wearing perfume makes a good impression on those he deals with. Once per post-battle sequence, he may deduct D6 dinars from the price of any single item he buys, to a minimum of 1 dinar.

extra_items.why: Relics of the Crusades pp. 4 and 16: 20+D6 dinars, Rare 9, sold only at Dimashque (William, 21 Nov 2026: "Relics yes, bring items and skills and spells in")

extra_items.name: Robe of Honour
extra_items.flavour: Generally granted to those who excel in the service of a Sultan or Caliph, a robe of honour would increase its wearer’s reputation dramatically.
extra_items.note: Heroes only. Not available to warbands on the Path of Sigmar or the Path of the Worm, nor to a warband with a member barred from Dimashque.

rules.text: Warriors flock to join the warband. You may re-roll a D6 when seeing how experienced potential henchmen are when recruiting.

extra_items.why: Relics of the Crusades pp. 4 and 16, its heading printed Robe of Honor: 50+2D6 dinars, Rare 10, sold only at Dimashque; its restrictions name paths, not warband types, so the note says them (William, 21 Nov 2026: "Relics yes, bring items and skills and spells in")

extra_items.name: Standard of Sigmar
extra_items.flavour: This grand standard displayed the two-headed hammer in red on a white background. The sight of it flying over the battlefield steeled the hearts of those loyal to Sigmar.

rules.text: The standard requires one hand to use and can be carried by any Hero in the warband. While the Hero carrying it is still alive, the warband adds +1 to its Leadership for rout tests.

extra_items.why: Relics of the Crusades pp. 3 and 16: 60+2D6 dinars, Rare 9, sold only at Tyrius; Path of Sigmar only, a path rather than a warband type, so the note says so (William, 21 Nov 2026: "Relics yes, bring items and skills and spells in")

extra_items.name: Wash Bar
extra_items.flavour: Another invention from Araby that is now common amongst the higher classes of the Old World. Wash bars were used to keep the bodies of Arabians clean during their various religious rituals.

rules.text: A wash bar lasts for D6 games and must be used in every post-battle sequence. Its user may add or deduct 1 from his rolls on the Serious Injuries chart.

extra_items.why: Relics of the Crusades pp. 4 and 16: 5+D6 dinars, Rare 6, sold only at Dimashque (William, 21 Nov 2026: "Relics yes, bring items and skills and spells in")

extra_items.name: Sharab
extra_items.flavour: The tinkle of the sharab sellers can be heard in most bazaars in Araby. These cold drinks of concentrated fruit would later come to the Old World under the names of ‘sirops’ or ‘sorbets’.

rules.text: A warrior can spend a turn drinking sharab, and then ignores the Hot scenario rule for 2D6 turns. If he is affected by burning sands, he must drink it before the battle begins, and the 2D6 turns begin from turn 1. There is only enough sharab for one use.

extra_items.why: Relics of the Crusades pp. 4 and 16: 30+3D6 dinars, Rare 8, sold only at Dimashque (William, 21 Nov 2026: "Relics yes, bring items and skills and spells in")

extra_items.name: Khufa Beans
extra_items.flavour: A shepherd once noticed his goats becoming more lively after grazing on the beans from the Khufa plant. He suffered the same effect when he crushed the beans and mixed them with milk. This potion soon became a common drink throughout Araby.

rules.text: A warband that indulges in a jug of khufa before a scenario may re-roll any failed Initiative tests until the next battle begins. There are only enough khufa beans for one use.

extra_items.why: Relics of the Crusades pp. 4-5 and 17: 20+2D6 dinars, Rare 7 at Dimashque (Rare 8 at Khalibon, in the note) (William, 21 Nov 2026: "Relics yes, bring items and skills and spells in")

extra_items.name: Dwarf Helm
extra_items.flavour: Invented by dwarfs to aid their work in the mines, a dwarf helm allows its bearer to see well in darkness and to also keep both hands free.

rules.text: A model equipped with a dwarf helm has a special 4+ save on a D6 against being stunned. If the save is made, treat the stunned result as knocked down instead. This save is not modified by the opponent's Strength.
A warrior equipped with a dwarf helm counts as wearing a helmet lit by a torch, and keeps both hands free.

extra_items.why: Relics of the Crusades pp. 3 and 17: 10+2D6 dinars, Rare 8, sold only at Tyrius; it counts as a helmet, so the helmet's Avoid Stun (William, 21 Nov 2026: "Relics yes, bring items and skills and spells in")

extra_items.name: Abacus
extra_items.flavour: An abacus is made up of beads threaded along rows of rods. It is very helpful for mathematical calculations and is commonly used by experienced merchants.

rules.text: A character using an abacus looks extremely experienced when dealing with the average trader. He may re-roll one D6 when using the Haggle skill.

extra_items.why: Relics of the Crusades pp. 4 and 17: 15+2D6 dinars, Rare 8, sold only at Dimashque (William, 21 Nov 2026: "Relics yes, bring items and skills and spells in")

extra_items.name: Arabian Steed

rules.text: An Arabian steed is an Elven steed that may be ridden by humans.

extra_items.why: Relics of the Crusades p. 4: 90 dinars, Rare 10, sold only at Dimashque, "as Elven Steed, but may be ridden by humans", so the Elven Steed's profile and Battle Schooled; a mount, so its beast is in apps/bestiary/data/bestiary.json (William, 21 Nov 2026: "Relics yes, bring items and skills and spells in")

extra_items.name: House
extra_items.flavour: Houses were generally for sale in any town in Araby, as long as you could gain the permission of the ruler. They offered quite a lot of comforts compared to other forms of accommodation.
extra_items.note: Dimashque: 60+D6x10 dinars, Rare 8. Khalibon: 60+4D6 dinars, Rare 9.

rules.text: The warband gains the benefits of a town's citizens. When it sells treasure it counts as one size smaller, so a warband of 10-12 members counts as 7-9. Note the town the house is bought in: the warband gains +1 to any rarity roll when trading there.

extra_items.why: Relics of the Crusades pp. 3-5 and 17, a dwelling: 50+5D6 dinars, Rare 7 at Tyrius (Dimashque's and Khalibon's prices in the note); its rules move here from the campaign rules' Dwellings (William, 21 Nov 2026: "Relics yes, bring items and skills and spells in")

extra_items.name: Shoppe
extra_items.flavour: A shoppe was basically a two story house, with the ground level used to sell things.
extra_items.note: Dimashque: 60+2D6 dinars, Rare 7. Khalibon: 50+2D6 dinars, Rare 10.

rules.text: The warband must own a house before buying a shoppe. It sells used equipment for 75% of its original cost, and adds 2D6 dinars to its treasury after every game. A Hero with the Smith (Academic) skill becomes an Inventor, as the Path of Knowledge advance.

extra_items.why: Relics of the Crusades pp. 3-5 and 17, a dwelling: 60+2D6 dinars, Rare 8 at Tyrius (Dimashque's and Khalibon's in the note); its rules move here from the campaign rules' Dwellings (William, 21 Nov 2026: "Relics yes, bring items and skills and spells in")

extra_items.name: Temple
extra_items.flavour: The lives of those who built temples to Sigmar were constantly filled with a steady stream of worshippers to their doors. Because of this they were constantly reminded of their duties and could not stray from the light.

rules.text: The warband may only build a temple if it owns a house. A warrior casting a Divine Intervention gains +1 to the attempt. The leader gains the Good Shepherd ability, which works much as the Children of the Horned Rat spell, bringing D3 hammer-wielding zealots from the Witch Hunter warband list in place of the rats.

extra_items.why: Relics of the Crusades pp. 3-4 and 17, a dwelling: 150+D6x25 dinars, Rare 9 at Tyrius (Dimashque's in the note); its rules move here from the campaign rules' Dwellings (William, 21 Nov 2026: "Relics yes, bring items and skills and spells in")

extra_items.name: Arabian Tent
extra_items.flavour: Arabian tents were majestic constructions that offered the comforts of city dwellings in the wilderness. A well made tent was hard to come by, as the desert nomads that make them were a surly, blasphemous lot.

rules.text: The warband is friends with the desert nomads. Its leader adds +1 to his Initiative when testing whether the warband is lost in the desert. If that test's roll is a 1, a merchant approaches and the warband may trade using Khalibon's trading chart.

extra_items.why: Relics of the Crusades pp. 4-5 and 17, a dwelling: 60+2D6 dinars, Rare 12 at Dimashque (Rare 11 at Khalibon, in the note); its rules move here from the campaign rules' Dwellings (William, 21 Nov 2026: "Relics yes, bring items and skills and spells in")

extra_items.name: Howdah

rules.name: Howdah
rules.text: A howdah may be fitted to any great beast. The beast then follows every special rule for a cart (Vehicles of the Empire), except as below.

rules.name: Movement
rules.text: The beast moves and runs at its own Movement, at -1 for every passenger after the first. It may turn up to 90 degrees in its movement phase without penalty; if it turns further, it moves at half pace and may not charge that turn.

rules.name: Out of Control
rules.text: The beast goes out of control only if it fails a Leadership test, which it may take on its driver's Leadership.

rules.name: Combat
rules.text: The beast charges as normal. A passenger fights in close combat only with a thrusting weapon (a mancatcher, spear or halberd, for instance) and only from the space of the howdah nearest the enemy.

rules.name: Shooting
rules.text: Passengers may shoot at enemies engaged with the beast.

extra_items.why: the Marienburg Annual p. 10 (New Vehicles): 80 gc, Rare 10, for any great beast, so for everyone; a vehicle bought as an item, as the Skeleton Chariot and the Mortis Engine are (William, 23 Nov 2026: "Add the Howdah if it is an item a warband buys"). The page's Chariot is not added
